title: File the close letter at the moment of close
action: Per D2 (store id aedb5be9): every bee close files its close letter immediately, attended sessions included. In mailbox.rs, split file_run_letter's compose-and-file core from its armed gate (anchor mailbox.rs:1754 'if !armed(root) {' / 1755 'return RunEnd::NotArmed;') and add pub(crate) fn file_close_letter(root: &Path, run: &str) -> RunEnd that runs the same core WITHOUT the armed gate. Also change file_run_letter so an EXISTING letter re-composes regardless of arming (advisor P1: check letter_files_for_run before the armed early-return; the existence check is names-only so an unarmed checkout with no letter still pays ~zero). Extend D12 recovery candidacy: a lettered run whose entries file mtime is newer than its letter file mtime is a candidate too (two stats, no opens; candidacy today is 'entries and NO letter', see silent_run_candidates / the lettered set near mailbox.rs:1992-2038). In drivers/close.rs, call file_close_letter fail-open INSIDE record_feature_close_in_mailbox (anchor close.rs:3075 'fn record_feature_close_in_mailbox', 3099 'mailbox::record_close_stop(') right after record_close_stop, using the SAME control root already resolved there — never the worktree root (advisor P2). A Failed outcome warns on stderr like record_run_end (mailbox.rs:1800-1808) and never refuses the close. Write tests per the plan's ld-1 triad; judge existing coverage in mailbox.rs and work.rs tests first and author only the gap.

truths: An attended (unarmed) bee close leaves a filed letter with close sections in .bee/human-mailbox/
A later run end re-composes that same file: one letter, filed_at and read status preserved, post-close entries included
A close-lettered run that goes silent with newer entries is still recovered by the D12 pass

artifacts.substantive: file_close_letter plus unarmed re-compose of existing letters plus mtime-based recovery candidacy, with tests

key_links: record_feature_close_in_mailbox calls file_close_letter at the control root after record_close_stop
prohibitions: No second letter file for one run (D11)
Run-end filing for a run with NO letter stays gated on armed() (D9)
Close is never refused because of a letter failure (fail-open, D10)
